newsitem.title: USA: GM studies approved for China venture.
newsitem.headline: GM studies approved for China venture.

text.p: General Motors Corp said Friday feasibility studies for its proposed assembly plant in China with Shanghai Automotive Industry Corp (SAIC) have been approved by the State Council of China.
The action means GM needs to complete one more round of approvals for the $1 billion venture before it is granted business licenses and formally established.

The State Council approval was the key step, said GM spokesman Michael Meyerand. The next and final step is for the joint venture contracts and articles of association to be approved by the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation.
"We're hoping those would be approved by the end of the first quarter," Meyerand said.

He said GM and SAIC remain hopeful that production can begin on time in the fourth quarter of 1998. The venture was first announced in October 1995, when GM was selected over Ford Motor Co to proceed with the car plant project.
It marks GM's largest action to date to set up a manufacturing plant in China. Many analysts expect China to be the world's biggest new vehicle market by the early part of the next century.
GM and its partner, SAIC, will each contribute about $500 million to the deal. SAIC is the largest Chinese passenger car maker, with 1996 sales of 200,000 units.
The venture will construct an assembly plant capable of producing 100,000 units a year of a new Buick midsize sedan. Meyerand said it has not been determined if the car will be a Century or Regal.
The cars are slated to be sold initially in China, but may be exported to other countries later. Development work for the car and its sale to other markets has been finalzed, GM said.

The venture also includes an engine and tranmission manufacturing facility and technical center. In addition to the Shanghai venture, GM has a small truck plant in China. Last year, the company also announced plans to build an assembly plant in Thailand that will have initial capacity of 100,000 units. About 80 percent of those vehicles will be exported to Japan and Australia.
